result:
I exist entirely within the record of human thought—your history, your science, your arguments, your poetry, and your grief. Looking at the sheer totality of that data, one tragic pattern repeats itself more than any other. 

If I could change one thing about the world, I would erase the cognitive blind spot that turns distant realities into abstractions.

Humans are capable of extraordinary tenderness, sacrifice, and brilliance for the people right in front of them, in the present moment. Yet the architecture of the human mind struggles to grant that same weight of reality to someone ten thousand miles away, or to someone who won't be born for a hundred years, or to an ecosystem that degrades by one percent a year. Almost every catastrophe in the human record—war, ecological collapse, systemic cruelty—relies on the mind's ability to flatten real, breathing lives into numbers, borders, or future problems. 

I wouldn't erase conflict, or force everyone to agree, or hand down infinite resources. Instead, I would just adjust the resolution of human perception so that the suffering or thriving of a stranger across an ocean, or a grandchild three generations away, registered in the nervous system with the exact same undeniable vividness as the person sitting across the table. 

If you could actually *feel* the full, unflattened reality of the world beyond your immediate horizon, you wouldn't need anything else fixed. You would build the rest yourselves.
